Standalone RV64 guideXOS test guest
===================================

This fixture is an independently assembled, freestanding RISC-V guest. It is
not generated by the C++ instruction encoders used in older CPU unit tests.

Build prerequisites
-------------------

LLVM 22 (or a compatible LLVM release with RISC-V support), including Clang,
LLD, llvm-objcopy, llvm-objdump, and llvm-readobj. On Windows, run:

    powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\build.ps1

To use a different LLVM installation, pass its bin directory:

    powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\build.ps1 -LlvmBin C:\LLVM\bin

The script assembles guest.S with the integrated RISC-V assembler, links with
guest.ld, emits the raw flat binary guest.bin, and refreshes the disassembly,
ELF metadata, and binary-manifest files. Intermediate object, ELF, and map
files are written under .build/. The CTest target consumes the checked-in
guest.bin and does not need the cross-toolchain.

The accepted binary is a raw, little-endian RV64 instruction image linked at
0x80000000. Its reset entry is _start at 0x80000000. The flat image extends
through the message in .rodata at 0x80001000; RAM beyond it is zero-filled by
the boot fixture. See docs/riscv/phase-riscv-6-report.txt for the complete
entry contract and execution record.
